query: Which method can be used for concurrent strength–ductility improvement, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Applying controlled thermomechanical processing (cold working followed by intermediate-temperature annealing with optimized parameters) on a conventional alloy will induce a heterogeneous (bimodal) grain structure that concurrently improves both yield strength and ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: A conventionally processed alloy with a homogeneous, equiaxed grain structure.
generation.intervention: Use cold working followed by an annealing treatment at an intermediate temperature with controlled cooling rate and strain rate settings.
generation.conditions: Processing parameters (temperature, strain rate, cooling rate) are precisely optimized to induce partial recrystallization that yields a mix of fine and coarse grains; the treatment should be performed under conditions where excessive grain growth is avoided.
generation.structural_mediator: A bimodal grain distribution consisting of fine grains for strengthening (via increased grain boundary area) and coarse grains for enhancing ductility by allowing greater strain accommodation.
generation.mechanism: The fine grains enhance strength through grain boundary strengthening while the coarse grains provide improved plasticity; the heterogeneous microstructure synergistically supports both properties concurrently.
generation.predicted_outcome: The alloy will exhibit a higher yield and ultimate strength as well as significantly improved ductility compared to the baseline homogeneous microstructure.
generation.baseline: The same alloy processed via conventional thermomechanical routes that produce a uniform grain size distribution.
generation.boundary: The improvement is expected primarily in alloys amenable to grain refinement and recovery processes; if the alloy composition or processing window does not support a controlled bimodal distribution, the method may not yield the desired dual improvement.
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude of strength and ductility enhancement depends on the exact processing parameter optimization and may vary with alloy composition; precise quantitative improvements are uncertain without systematic parameter study.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of identical alloy samples. Process one set using conventional thermomechanical treatment to produce a homogeneous microstructure (control) and the other set using the proposed controlled thermomechanical processing (cold working followed by an intermediate-temperature annealing with controlled cooling) aimed at producing a bimodal microstructure. Characterize the microstructure using electron microscopy and perform standard tensile tests.
measurements: Grain size distribution analysis (to confirm bimodal vs. homogeneous structure)
Yield strength and ultimate tensile strength measurements
Ductility evaluation via elongation or fracture strain
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples processed with the controlled thermomechanical treatment do not exhibit both a statistically significant increase in strength and ductility (in comparison to the conventional processing baseline), or if no bimodal grain structure is observed, then the hypothesis is falsified.

The tensile test specimen was machined from the bulk alloy ingot and is shown in Fig. 1b . The cast microstructure of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 is shown in Fig. 2a . Even in such a bulk cast ingot, a uniform and fine lamellar microstructure characteristic of eutectic alloys was achieved. The inter-lamellar spacing was about 2 μm. Unlike other conventional alloys based on a “principal element,” high-entropy alloy (HEA) is a unique material that maintains a random solid solution structure without forming intermetallic compounds in operating temperatures due to its high configurational entropy [1] – [3] . It also has outstanding physical and chemical properties, which makes it a potential replacement for traditional metallic materials, and it has recently been referred to as a multi-principal element alloy (MPEA) or compositionally concentrated alloy (CCA) [4] – [9] .

As attention in HEAs increases, many studies have been conducted to explore its mechanical, physical and chemical properties [10] – [15] . In particular, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA, which was the first developed HEA, is the most studied because of its excellent combination of tensile strength and elongation along with excellent fracture toughness and corrosion resistance [6] , [16] – [21] . chosen.conditions: optimized conditions (intermediate annealing temperatures and controlled cooling) that generate a dual-phase microstructure with fine and coarse grains
chosen.why: This method directly addresses the open question by experimentally establishing a processing route that induces a heterogeneous microstructure.
